question: What does AbbVie do, why is the stock priced at $286.20, and what is our exact New-Capital Verdict and Portfolio Action?

epigraph.quote: The rarest sight in biopharma is a company that loses its flagship drug to biosimilars and emerges three years later with higher revenues, wider margins, and a longer patent runway.
epigraph.author: Prologue — Post-LOE Underwriting

web_blocks.title: Executive Thesis: Business Quality First, Tape & Valuation Second

web_blocks.html: AbbVie Inc. (NYSE: ABBV) is a global biopharmaceutical leader. It generated $61.16 billion in FY2025 net revenues and guides to ~$67.8 billion in FY2026 (+10.9% YoY) [1, 3]. Separated from Abbott Laboratories in 2013, AbbVie executed one of the cleanest patent-cliff transitions in industry history. Skyrizi ($21.8B FY26E) and Rinvoq ($10.3B FY26E) now drive nearly half of total sales. Neuroscience ($13.0B FY26E) adds a second high-margin growth engine [3, 28]. Our price-blind audit (Chapters 1–6) assigns COMPOUNDER_PASS for business durability and PASS_WITH_WATCH for KPIs. That watch flag reflects $77B in pro forma post-Apogee debt, negative book equity (-$5.9B at Q2 2026), and 2027 IRA Medicare price cuts [1, 13, 27].

On the market tape at the November 20, 2026 close ($286.20, $505.89B market cap), ABBV trades at 17.60x forward P/E with a 2.54% forward dividend yield [3, 26]. The stock sits in a confirmed Stage 2 Volatility Contraction Pattern (5.44% Bollinger bandwidth, Daily RSI 49.19), just +1.75% above its 10-week EMA ($281.27) [26, 29]. However, the S&P 500 is in a Downtrend regime (38.0% breadth above 50-DMA, 10 distribution days). CMP ($286.20) offers 1.47:1 asymmetry versus 1.52:1–1.85:1 inside support. Our independent New-Capital Verdict is ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP into $277.05–$281.27, with a $340.00 base target (+18.8%) and a $249.53 invalidation stop. ABBV is NOT_HELD in the US portfolio (0 shares).

web_blocks.takeaway: ABBV combines rare post-LOE revenue acceleration (+10.9% YoY) with a tight Stage 2 consolidation, rewarding disciplined dip accumulation at $277.05–$281.27.

book_paragraphs: In 2023, AbbVie faced the moment every pharmaceutical investor dreads. Humira, a single biologic generating more than $21 billion a year at its peak, lost U.S. patent exclusivity to a wave of biosimilars. Most mega-cap drugmakers spend half a decade shrinking through a cliff of that size. AbbVie did the opposite. By 2025, total revenue rebounded to $61.16 billion. In October 2026, management raised full-year 2026 guidance to roughly $67.8 billion—more than $13 billion above the 2023 trough.

This monograph separates the business from the stock price before passing judgment. In Chapters 1 through 6, we audit AbbVie completely price-blind. We trace its evolution from the 2013 Abbott spin-off and examine the patient-level economics of Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Vraylar, Elahere, and Botox. We also walk through the $100 revenue-to-free-cash-flow waterfall, test the competitive moat, audit management's past promises, and inspect ten years of balance-sheet forensics. That audit earns a Compounder Pass, tempered by a Watch flag on $77 billion of pro forma post-Apogee debt and 2027 Medicare IRA price cuts.

Why does price-blind discipline matter? After a +31.89% six-month rally, it is tempting to chase momentum or dismiss the stock as expensive without checking the engine. By locking our view of business quality first, we know what we are buying. AbbVie is a dual-engine immunology and neuroscience franchise generating nearly $19 billion in annual free cash flow, paired with a balance sheet that demands steady debt paydown.

In Chapters 7 through 9, we examine the market tape. At $286.20, AbbVie trades at 17.60x forward earnings with a 2.54% forward dividend yield. The stock sits in a tight Stage 2 Volatility Contraction Pattern right above its 10-week EMA ($281.27). Because the S&P 500 is in a Downtrend regime (38.0% above 50-DMA), our verdict is Accumulate on Dip inside $277.05–$281.27. Our 12-to-18-month base target is $340.00, with a hard stop at $249.53. Since ABBV is not held in the portfolio, we keep marginal cash ready for a limit fill.

book_subsections.title: How to Use This Monograph: Separating the Business from the Tape
paragraphs: Most equity research mixes business quality and stock price in the opening paragraph, which anchors your judgment to whatever the market happened to do yesterday. We structure this book differently. Chapters 1 through 6 evaluate AbbVie as if it were a private company with no daily stock quote—examining how it survived the Humira cliff, how Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Vraylar, and Botox actually reach patients and clinics, how $100 of revenue turns into free cash flow, and whether management kept its past promises.

Only in Chapters 7 through 9 do we bring back the $286.20 share price, run a Reverse DCF to see what growth is already baked in, compare AbbVie against Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson, Merck, Bristol-Myers, and Gilead, and inspect the Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour charts. That separation is why our verdict is crisp: AbbVie passes the business test as a Compounder, and because it sits in a tight Stage 2 consolidation inside a weak broader market, disciplined investors should accumulate on dips into $277.05–$281.27 rather than chasing.

book_callouts.title: PROLOGUE SUMMARY: What You Need to Watch
book_callouts.text: Your thesis lives or dies on two numbers: Skyrizi and Rinvoq sustaining their >$32 billion trajectory while management pays down Apogee debt toward 2.0x net leverage, and ABBV holding above its rising 30-week average ($252.88 / $249.53 stop) through the 2027 IRA pricing cycle.
